title: Parity-driven RKKY decoupling and anomalous $1/R$ Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in $p$-wave magnets
abstract: Unconventional $p$-wave magnets, characterized by an odd-parity momentum-dependent spin splitting, offer a fundamentally distinct paradigm for non-collinear spintronics. Here, we theoretically investigate the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida indirect exchange in a two-dimensional $p$-wave magnet subjected to Rashba spin-orbit coupling. Using an analytical real-space Green's function formalism, we uncover a parity-driven spatial decoupling in the magnetic response. Because of the odd-parity exchange field, the out-of-plane Ising interaction is structurally insulated from the macroscopic $p$-wave modulation, oscillating isotropically at the shifted Fermi wavevector. Conversely, the in-plane Heisenberg components exhibit pronounced, directionally tunable spatial beating. Beyond collinear exchange, the hybridized bands generate a highly tunable, three-component Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction alongside symmetric off-diagonal anisotropies. We reveal that the out-of-plane chiral twisting is driven by the massive, nonrelativistic $p$-wave momentum shift, while the in-plane chiral components are strictly relativistic. Furthermore, the competition between the $p$-wave nodal geometry and the Rashba gap drives an anomalous, dimension-reducing crossover, in which the in-plane chiral components follow a 1D-like $1/R$ spatial decay along the nodal lines over an extended intermediate-distance window before ultimately recovering the conventional 2D $1/R^2$ asymptote. These findings establish $p$-wave magnets as promising platforms for engineering robust, directionally tunable non-collinear spin textures.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the RKKY interaction in $p$-wave magnets with Rashba SOC, revealing how odd parity fundamentally alters magnetic exchange. Key findings include a decoupling of out-of-plane Ising terms and the emergence of tunable DM interactions. The paper provides crucial insights into engineering robust, directionally controlled non-collinear spin textures.
main_problem: The study investigates how the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) indirect exchange interaction behaves in unconventional $p$-wave magnets when subjected to Rashba spin-orbit coupling.
main_result: The odd parity of the $p$-wave state causes a spatial decoupling of the out-of-plane Ising interaction, while the system generates a highly tunable, three-component Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction. Furthermore, an anomalous crossover leads to a dimension-reducing $1/R$ decay for in-plane chiral components.
method: The analysis employs an analytical real-space Green's function formalism and uses the stationary-phase approximation on momentum-space integrals to derive asymptotic expressions for the RKKY tensor components.
model_or_system: The model is a two-dimensional ($2D$) unconventional $p$-wave magnet described by an effective continuum Hamiltonian incorporating kinetic energy, an odd-parity momentum-dependent exchange field ($M_p\mathbf{k}$), and Rashba spin-orbit coupling ($\lambda$).
key_observables: RKKY exchange tensor components (Heisenberg, Ising, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction), spatial decay laws ($1/R$ vs $1/R^2$), and directional tunability of magnetic interactions.
important_parameters: Rashba coupling strength ($\lambda$), Fermi wavevector ($k_F$), and the momentum shift associated with the $p$-wave order.
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on long-distance asymptotic expressions for the Green's functions ($k_F R \gg 1$) and utilize an effective two-band continuum Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate RKKY interactions in $p$-wave magnets, showing constant-energy contours that reveal spin-splitting effects when RSOC is present. Later figures track the spatial dependence of various RKKY tensor components as a function of polarization angle.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical model and Hamiltonian to deriving the Green's functions using matrix inversion, then calculating the full RKKY exchange tensor via second-order perturbation theory in real space. The focus shifts to analyzing parity effects, decoupling mechanisms, and finally deriving closed-form asymptotic expressions for all interaction components.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of spin texture engineering through symmetry breaking (parity/RSOC) is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics, as these systems often involve engineered spin-orbit coupling or topological phases that dictate long-range interactions.
